blog.title: Designing with daylight
blog.description: The first decisions about light happen long before a fixture is chosen.
blog.body:
Daylight begins with orientation. A plan can place shared spaces where they receive the light their occupants use most, while utility rooms can take less exposed positions.

The size of an opening matters, but so do its depth, shading and the surfaces it illuminates. Testing these decisions together can make a room feel comfortable throughout the day.

A daylight study is also a conversation about glare, heat and privacy. The best solutions are shaped by local conditions and the needs of the people who use the space.
